definitions.gloss: to encourage; to hearten; to inspire courage in
definitions.explanation: To give someone courage or confidence, helping them feel braver or more motivated. A compound verb from 勇気 (courage) + づける (to give, to imbue with).

examples.japanese: {友達|ともだち}を{勇気|ゆうき}づけた。
{彼|かれ}の{言葉|ことば}に{勇気|ゆうき}づけられた。
examples.english: I was encouraged by his words.

examples.japanese: {落|お}ち{込|こ}んでいる{後輩|こうはい}を{勇気|ゆうき}づけるために{声|こえ}をかけた。
examples.english: I spoke to my junior to encourage them when they were feeling down.

notes:
USAGE:
{勇気|ゆうき}づける is an ichidan (ru-verb) that means to give someone courage. The passive form {勇気|ゆうき}づけられる (to be encouraged) is very common.

CONJUGATION:
- {勇気|ゆうき}づける (dictionary form)
- {勇気|ゆうき}づけない (negative)
- {勇気|ゆうき}づけた (past)
- {勇気|ゆうき}づけられる (passive — to be encouraged)

SIMILAR WORDS:
{励|はげ}ます also means to encourage, but has a broader scope and is more commonly used in everyday speech. {勇気|ゆうき}づける specifically emphasizes giving someone courage or bravery.
